channel.title: Reserve Bank of New Zealand News Releases
channel.description: Press releases issued by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand

item.title: New framework supports access to basic transaction services
item.description: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand – Te Pūtea Matua (RBNZ) has brought together public and private sector organisations to sign a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) aimed at supporting access to basic transaction services in New Zealand.

item.title: APRA and RBNZ complete joint bank stress test to promote trans-Tasman resilience
item.description: The Australian Prudential Regulation Authority (APRA) and the Reserve Bank of New Zealand – Te Pūtea Matua (RBNZ) have completed the 2026 Trans-Tasman Stress Test, their first joint stress testing exercise since 2017.

item.title: RBNZ and FMA outline supervisory expectations on cyber and AI risks
item.description: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand – Te Pūtea Matua (RBNZ) and the Financial Markets Authority – Te Mana Tātai Hokohoko (FMA) have today outlined their supervisory expectations on cyber risks associated with frontier Artificial Intelligence (AI).

item.title: Recruitment for two new Assistant Governors and Chief of Staff underway
item.description: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand – Te Pūtea Matua (RBNZ) has commenced recruitment for the two new roles of Assistant Governor Monetary Policy and Assistant Governor Payments and Cash.

item.title: Updates to the October Monetary Policy Review and November Financial Stability Report
item.description: We have updated the media conference and publication arrangements for the October 2026 MPR and the November 2026 FSR.

item.title: Consultation finds strong support for access to cash services
item.description: Today, we published findings from our Keeping Cash Local consultation about access to cash services, with new research on community views about cash services and cash use.

item.title: New Monetary Policy Committee member appointed
item.description: A new internal member of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), Rebecca Williams, has been appointed by the Minister of Finance, Nicola Willis, on the recommendation of the RBNZ Board.

item.title: Reserve Bank requests TSB to commission independent report
item.description: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand – Te Pūtea Matua is requesting an independent report from TSB under Section 95 of the Banking (Prudential Supervision) Act 1989.

item.title: RBNZ leaders visit Dunedin to understand how the local economy is evolving
item.description: Governor Anna Breman, alongside External Monetary Policy Committee member Prasanna Gai and Board Chair Rodger Finlay, visited Dunedin to meet with local communities and businesses from key sectors in the regional centre.

item.title: Reserve Bank welcomes findings of independent review of Covid-19 monetary policy
item.description: Board Chair Rodger Finlay has welcomed the findings of the Independent review of Covid-19 monetary policy released today by the Minister of Finance.

item.title: Māori access to capital (MA2K) snapshot 2026
item.description: Te Pūtea Matua – Reserve Bank of New Zealand has today published the 2026 Māori Access to Capital (MA2K) Snapshot, providing an updated industry-level view of Māori access to capital across participating banks, alongside the latest available aggregate system-level information.

item.title: Exploring the future of banking in New Zealand
item.description: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand – Te Pūtea Matua (RBNZ) has today published a Future of Banking study exploring how banking in New Zealand could evolve over the next decade.

item.title: Reserve Bank announces leadership changes as Assistant Governor Karen Silk prepares to depart
item.description: Reserve Bank of New Zealand – Te Pūtea Matua Assistant Governor Money Karen Silk will leave the Bank in December, after more than four years with the organisation.

item.title: RBNZ to regulate and supervise the High Value Clearing System
item.description: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand – Te Pūtea Matua will now regulate and supervise the High Value Clearing System, under the Financial Market Infrastructures Act 2021. This follows the Minister of Finance’s decision to designate the system on the Reserve Bank’s recommendation.

item.title: Reserve Bank releases near-final DTA standards and licensing questions for regulated deposit takers
item.description: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand – Te Pūtea Matua has published near-final versions of four Deposit Takers Act 2023 (DTA) standards, consultation submissions, and the questions that existing banks and non-bank deposit takers will need to answer if they are applying for a DTA licence.

item.title: Securing the future: the role of the repo market
item.description: In a speech delivered today at the KangaNews Debt Capital Markets Summit in Auckland, Reserve Bank Assistant Governor Money, Karen Silk, highlighted the growing importance of the repo market in supporting financial market liquidity, monetary policy implementation, and financial system resilience.

item.title: RBNZ approves entry of first non-bank member to Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS)
item.description: This follows the completion of the ESAS Access Review which was conducted to assess whether the 30-year access criteria were still fit for purpose in a rapidly changing finance eco-system.

item.title: OCR increased by 25 basis points to 2.75%
item.description: Monetary Policy Statement media release and the MPC’s Record of Meeting, which summarises the committee's discussions.

item.title: RBNZ explores issues facing New Zealand's payments system
item.description: We are seeking feedback on the issues we have identified with our payments system, and the proposed areas of work needed to address these.

item.title: Reserve Bank maintains Loan-to-Value Ratio (LVR) settings
item.description: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand – Te Pūtea Matua’s Financial Policy Committee (FPC) has decided to maintain current LVR settings in its annual review of macroprudential policy.

item.title: RBNZ outlines priorities for a resilient and enabling financial system
item.description: Assistant Governor Financial Stability Angus McGregor highlighted the importance of financial stability and outlined priorities shaping our prudential regulation approach in remarks delivered today at the Financial Services Council Conference.

item.title: Strong relationships maintained in latest RBNZ Relationship Charter survey
item.description: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand Te Pūtea Matua's engagement with regulated entities continues to be based on strong relationships, according to the results of the 2026 Relationship Charter survey. In this year’s survey, 89% of respondents rated their relationship with the Reserve Bank as ‘good’ or ‘very good.’

item.title: Consultation on a prudential levy opens
item.description: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand – Te Pūtea Matua has today released a consultation document on the introduction of a prudential levy. This consultation is being undertaken on behalf of the Minister of Finance. This initiative was announced as part of the Government’s Budget 2026.

item.title: RBNZ leadership continues regional engagement to hear first-hand economic perspectives in Nelson-Tasman
item.description: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) Governor Dr Anna Breman, Board Member Jeremy Banks, External Monetary Policy Committee Member Carl Hansen, and Director of Stakeholder Engagement Naomi Mitchell have travelled to Nelson-Tasman to engage with local businesses, industries, and communities as part of the RBNZ's regional leadership engagement programme.

item.title: Strong public interest in cash consultation
item.description: The Keeping Cash Local consultation has now closed with nearly 6000 responses received, and findings are expected to be released in late September.

item.title: RBNZ Deputy Chair appointed
item.description: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand – Te Pūtea Matua welcomes the elevation of Byron Pepper to the role of Deputy Chair of its Board. Mr Pepper was appointed by the Governor-General on the recommendation of the Minister of Finance for a term of four years, from 20 July 2026 to his current term end date of 30 June 2030.

item.title: Speech by Paul Conway: Finding signal in the inflation noise
item.description: In a speech delivered today at an event hosted by BusinessNZ in Wellington, Chief Economist, Paul Conway, discussed the fallout from the conflict in the Middle East, and how inflation expectations and price-setting behaviour will influence the path of interest rates as we return inflation back to our 2% target midpoint.

item.title: OCR increased to 2.50% to return inflation to 2%
item.description: Monetary Policy Review media release and the MPC’s Record of Meeting, which summarises the committee's discussions, leading to the decision.

item.title: RBNZ appoints Assistant Governor Financial Stability
item.description: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Governor Anna Breman has appointed Angus McGregor as Assistant Governor Financial Stability following an extensive recruitment process.

item.title: DTA consultations on crisis preparedness and final tranche of draft standards
item.description: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) - Te Pūtea Matua has opened consultations on six draft standards and a package of crisis preparedness policies for deposit takers. The consultations are the latest step in RBNZ’s implementation of the most significant regulatory reform for the sector in decades, the Deposit Takers Act 2023 (DTA).

item.title: ASB Bank ordered to pay $6.731 million in largest AML/CFT penalty to date
item.description: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand – Te Pūtea Matua welcomes the High Court’s decision to impose a civil pecuniary penalty of $6.731 million on ASB Bank Limited.

item.title: RBNZ announces decision on use of the word 'bank'
item.description: All New Zealand deposit takers licensed under the DTA will be able to call themselves banks.

item.title: Cash consultation alternate formats and additional information published
item.description: Alternate formats of the Keeping Cash Local consultation document and survey – in NZSL, Braille, Easy Read, Audio and Large Print – are now available for disabled people and their communities to have their say.

item.title: RBNZ Governor connects with Hawke's Bay on Monetary Policy
item.description: On Friday 29 May, Reserve Bank of New Zealand Governor, Dr Anna Breman, spoke to rural and primary sector leaders in the Hawke’s Bay discussing insights from the May 2026 Monetary Policy Statement.

item.title: Prudential Levy Consultation
item.description: As part of the Government’s Budget 2026 the Minister of Finance announced the Government’s intention to introduce a prudential levy under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 2021 (RBNZ Act).

item.title: Reserve Bank files High Court action against The Co-operative Bank
item.description: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand – Te Pūtea Matua (RBNZ) has filed civil proceedings in the Wellington High Court against The Co-operative Bank Limited.

item.title: OCR held at 2.25%
item.description: Monetary Policy Statement media release and the MPC’s Record of Meeting, which summarises the committee's discussions.

item.title: Financial system resilient amid heightened global risks
item.description: “The global risk environment has worsened over the past six months, as conflict in the Middle East threatens world energy supply”, says Reserve Bank Governor Anna Breman in publishing the Financial Stability Report this morning. “However, New Zealand’s financial system is resilient and well positioned to support households and businesses even if economic conditions soften."

item.title: Enhanced Monetary Policy Committee transparency changes announced
item.description: The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) and the Minister of Finance have agreed changes to the MPC Charter that will provide more transparency and accountability of MPC decision-making.

item.title: RBNZ Governor engages Waikato community on economic outlook
item.description: On Wednesday 29 April, Governor Dr Anna Breman spoke with a range of business owners, young professionals, and local leaders in Hamilton as part of her regional engagement programme.

item.title: Cash consultation legal basis and ongoing industry engagement
item.description: We are releasing additional information about the legal basis of the Keeping Cash Local consultation proposal to help people respond to the consultation.

item.title: RBNZ opens consultation on draft changes to insurance prudential legislation
item.description: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) - Te Pūtea Matua has opened consultation on an exposure draft of a Bill that amends the Insurance (Prudential Supervision) Act 2010 (IPSA).

item.title: Cash consultation continues, update on further supporting information
item.description: Assistant Governor Money Karen Silk encourages the public to have their say about local access to withdraw cash, deposit cash and swap cash for low-denomination banknotes and coins.

item.title: OCR on hold at 2.25%
item.description: Monetary Policy Review media release and the MPC’s Record of Meeting, which summarises the committee's discussions, leading to the decision.

item.title: Recruitment for Assistant Governor, Financial Stability underway
item.description: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand - Te Pūtea Matua has commenced recruitment for the role of Assistant Governor Financial Stability.

item.title: Why New Zealanders still feel squeezed despite lower inflation
item.description: Chief Economist Paul Conway delivers a keynote speech at the National Financial Advisers Conference 2026 in Auckland, with this year’s focus titled “Purchasing power and the real cost of living in New Zealand.

item.title: RBNZ Governor discusses impact of Middle East conflict on NZ economy
item.description: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) is well positioned to handle the challenges to our price stability and financial stability mandates caused by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

item.title: Expanded April Monetary Policy Review and change to focus of Business NZ speech
item.description: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand – Te Pūtea Matua is expanding its communications approach for the 8 April Monetary Policy Review.

item.title: RBNZ releases Summary of Submissions and Key Decisions from Liquidity Management Consultation
item.description: The Reserve Bank has published a Summary of Submissions and Key Decisions paper on the Liquidity Management Review consultation. Decisions on the design of Open Market Operations (OMO) are expected to come into effect from 2 April 2026.

item.title: RBNZ working with industry to improve access to basic transaction services
item.description: Last year the Council of Financial Regulators (CoFR) consulted the public on whether New Zealanders should have the right to access a basic transaction account if they want one.
